title: Vero overview
description: Health, traffic, latency and errors for every Vero service, plus the live features and the AI worker.

panels.title: Instance health
panels.description: Every running copy of every service, left to right over the selected time range. Green means Prometheus could read its /metrics; red means it could not. Each service runs as a primary and a replica behind nginx, so one red row does not always mean users noticed.

panels.title: Requests per second
panels.description: HTTP requests answered by all selected services, averaged over the scrape window. Excludes Prometheus's own scrapes.

panels.title: Server errors
panels.description: Share of requests answered with a 5xx status. Under 1% is normal; above 5% for five minutes raises the HighServerErrorRate alert.

panels.title: p95 latency
panels.description: 95 of every 100 requests finished faster than this. Amber from 300 ms, red from 1 s.

panels.title: Chat connections
panels.description: Socket.io connections open to chat-service right now, across replicas. Roughly one per open browser tab.

panels.title: Notes open for editing
panels.description: Live Yjs collaboration sockets in notes-service: one per person per open note.

panels.title: Meetings in progress
panels.description: Mediasoup rooms held in memory by meet-service. Shows 0 when meet is not running.

panels.title: Requests per second by service
panels.description: How busy each service is. Replicas are added together. A line dropping to zero while the others carry on usually means that service stopped.

panels.title: Responses by status
panels.description: Every response grouped by its status class. 4xx is usually the client (expired session, missing item); 5xx is a server fault.

panels.title: Response time, all services
panels.description: p50 is a typical request, p95 a slow one, p99 the slowest 1 in 100. The gap between p50 and p99 is how uneven the experience is.

panels.title: p95 response time by service
panels.description: Which service is slow. Notes can spike while an AI summary is being written; that waits on Gemini, not the database.

panels.title: Slowest routes
panels.description: The ten routes with the highest p95 over the selected time range, with how often each was called. Routes are shown as written in the code (/tasks/:id), not as individual URLs. Health checks are left out.

targets.expr: topk(10, (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service, method, route, le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"vero|vero-meet", service=~"$service", route!="unmatched", route!~".*health"}[$__range]))) > 0))

sum by (service, method, route) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"vero|vero-meet", service=~"$service", route!="unmatched", route!~".*health"}[$__range])) and on (service, method, route) topk(10, (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service, method, route, le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"vero|vero-meet", service=~"$service", route!="unmatched", route!~".*health"}[$__range]))) > 0))

defaults.noValue: No requests in this time range

panels.title: Server errors per second by service
panels.description: 5xx responses only. Empty is good.

panels.title: Routes returning server errors
panels.description: Every route that answered with a 5xx in the selected time range, most errors first. Check that service's log in .dev-logs/ for the stack trace.

targets.expr: sum by (service, method, route, code) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{code=~"5..", job=~"vero|vero-meet", service=~"$service"}[$__range])) > 0

defaults.noValue: No server errors in this time range

panels.title: Chat
panels.description: Open sockets (line, left axis) and messages sent per minute (bars, right axis).

panels.title: Notes collaboration
panels.description: People with a note open in the live editor. Each open note in each tab counts once.

panels.title: Meetings
panels.description: Rooms in progress (left axis) and people connected to them (right axis). Empty when meet-service is not running.

panels.title: Notifications delivered
panels.description: Notifications sent per minute by channel. Red bars are deliveries that failed (SMTP refused, push endpoint error). Expired push subscriptions are cleaned up and not counted as failures.

panels.title: AI jobs per minute
panels.description: Note digests finished by the AI worker. Rejected means an expected refusal (no GEMINI_API_KEY, malformed input) returned to the user; crashed means an unexpected error that BullMQ will retry.

panels.title: AI job duration
panels.description: Time from the worker picking up a job to finishing it. Most of it is waiting on Gemini, so long notes take longer.

defaults.noValue: No AI jobs in this time range

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Resident memory of each service, replicas added together. A line that only ever climbs is worth a look.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU time used per second. 100% is one full core.

panels.title: Event loop delay (p99)
panels.description: How long JavaScript work waited for its turn. Above about 100 ms everything in that service feels slow at once, usually from synchronous work on a request.
